Turkish politician who rose from Istanbul mayor to prime minister (2003–2014) and has been president since 2014, co-founding the AKP. His rule has drawn criticism for democratic backsliding. Who is he?
Recep Tayyip Erdoğan: President of Turkey since 2014. Recep Tayyip Erdoğan (born 26 February 1954) is a Turkish politician and statesman who has been the president of Turkey since 2014.
The first person to walk to both the North and South Poles, this explorer later led his son on a 600-mile renewable-energy-only trek to the South Pole in 2017 — who is he?
A key figure in Japan's Meiji Restoration, this samurai later led a doomed 1877 uprising against the very government he helped create, dying in the fighting — who was he?
Saigō Takamori: Japanese samurai and politician (1828–1877)

Angered by how territory was divided after an earlier 1912-13 conflict, Bulgaria attacked its former allies Serbia and Greece in mid-1913, only to be beaten back on multiple fronts as Romania invaded from the north and the Ottomans reclaimed lost ground — which conflict?
Second Balkan War: Bulgaria's invasion of its neighbours (1913)
Dubbed the 'Father of Japanese capitalism,' this Meiji-era business magnate founded the country's first joint-stock bank and the Tokyo Stock Exchange — who is he?
The 33rd king and founder of the Tibetan Empire, he formally brought Buddhism to Tibet, built the Jokhang, and moved his capital to Lhasa while his minister devised the Tibetan script. Who was he?
Songtsen Gampo: 1st Tibetan Emperor and 33rd King of Tibet (d.650)

After her husband was arrested ahead of Belarus's 2020 election, this activist entered the presidential race in his place — a decision the regime allowed, wrongly assuming a woman couldn't mount a real challenge — who is she?
Sparked by the drowning of King Henry I's only legitimate son in the White Ship disaster, this 1138–1153 English succession war pitted Empress Matilda against Stephen of Blois — what is it called?
The Anarchy: Civil war in England and Normandy (1138–1153)
As first Grand Inquisitor of the Spanish Inquisition from 1478, this Dominican friar was also a chief supporter of the decree expelling Jews from Spain — who was he?
Tomás de Torquemada: Grand Inquisitor of Spain (1420–1498)

Going by VGE, this finance-minister-turned-president eked out a 1974 win over François Mitterrand with 50.8% of the vote, then liberalized French law on divorce, contraception, and abortion — who was he?
Valéry Giscard d'Estaing: President of France from 1974 to 1981.
Serving under Jimmy Carter, this Minnesota senator became the 42nd U.S. vice president and the Democratic Party's presidential nominee in 1984 — who is he?
Walter Mondale: Vice President of the United States from 1977 to 1981.

Dubbed 'the Great Commoner' and 'the Boy Orator' for his faith in ordinary people and his thundering rhetoric, this Nebraskan was the Democrats' presidential nominee three times — in 1896, 1900, and 1908. Who was he?
This retired Turkish general served as the 30th Chief of the General Staff of the Turkish Armed Forces before becoming Minister of National Defense — who is he?
Yaşar Güler: Turkish general and politician (born 1954)
Son of Edward the Elder, this ruler is regarded by modern historians as the first King of England; he never married and was succeeded by his half-brother Edmund — who is he?
Æthelstan: King of the English from 927 to 939.
Who among these was born first?
Levi Strauss (born 1829) is the earliest of the four.
Who among these was born first?
Benjamin Banneker (born 1731) is the earliest of the four.
Who among these four was born earliest?
Zhuge Liang (born 181) is the earliest of the four. After helping found Shu Han, Zhuge Liang exercised near-total authority over both civil and military affairs.
Which of these four is the oldest?
MUMPS (founded 1966) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four appeared earliest?
Pascal (programming language) (published 1972) is the earliest of the four.
Pick the physicist from these four.
Wernher von Braun is a physicist. As a young man, von Braun worked in Nazi Germany's rocket development program.
Which one below is best known as a chemist?
Willard Libby is a chemist. For his contributions to the team that developed this process, Libby was awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1960.
What is the atomic number of Oxygen?
Oxygen is a chemical element; it has the symbol O and its atomic number is 8.
In what year was Frank Oppenheimer born?
Frank Oppenheimer: The younger brother of renowned physicist J.
In what year was Omar Khayyam born?
Omar Khayyam (1048–1131) was a Persian poet and polymath, known for his contributions to mathematics, astronomy, philosophy, and Persian literature.
In what year was Marie Curie born?
Marie Curie: Curie was born in Warsaw, Russian Empire, where she studied at the clandestine Flying University and began her practical scientific training.
In what year did António de Oliveira Salazar die?
António de Oliveira Salazar: The regime he created lasted until 1974, making it one of the longest-lived authoritarian dictatorships in modern Europe.
In what year did Josef Mengele die?
Josef Mengele: Before the war, Mengele received doctorates in anthropology and medicine, and he began a career as a researcher.
In what year was HIV discovered?
HIV: Without treatment, the average survival time after infection with HIV is estimated to be 9 to 11 years, depending on the HIV subtype.
In what year was Platinum discovered?
Platinum is a chemical element; it has symbol Pt and atomic number 78.
Rituximab: Pfizer. It is given by slow intravenous infusion.
Which country is Grumman F-14 Tomcat from?

Grumman F-14 Tomcat: United States. The Grumman F-14 Tomcat is an American carrier-capable supersonic, twin-engine, tandem two-seat, twin-tail, all-weather-capable variable-sweep wing fighter aircraft.
Who is credited with discovering Thorium?
Thorium: Jöns Jacob Berzelius. Thorium is a chemical element; it has symbol Th and atomic number 90.
Who is credited with discovering Cauchy–Schwarz inequality?
Cauchy–Schwarz inequality: Viktor Bunyakovsky. It is considered one of the most important and widely used inequalities in mathematics.
Who is credited with discovering Phosphorus?
Phosphorus: Hennig Brand. Phosphorus is a chemical element; it has symbol P and atomic number 15.

This alternative-medicine practice, a component of traditional Chinese medicine, involves inserting thin needles into the body, though its underlying theories are considered pseudoscientific by mainstream science — what's the practice called?
Acupuncture is a form of alternative medicine and a component of traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) in which thin needles are inserted into the body.
This large, muscular mastiff-type dog breed descends from ancestors brought to the British North American colonies, where they worked on small farms and ranches — what's the breed?
American Bulldog is a large, muscular breed of mastiff-type dog.
Known as 'doodlebugs' for the trails they leave in sand, these insect larvae dig pits to ambush wandering ants, while the winged adults are often mistaken for dragonflies — what are they?
Antlion are a group of about 2,000 species of insect in the neuropteran family Myrmeleontidae.

The third-largest member of its family behind the Siberian taimen and Pacific Chinook, this anadromous fish hatches in rivers, matures at sea, and changes color and appearance when it returns upstream to spawn — name this fish?
Atlantic salmon (Salmo salar) is a species of ray-finned fish in the family Salmonidae.
This steroid medication treats conditions ranging from rheumatoid arthritis and psoriasis to asthma, and is also given before preterm birth to help speed a baby's lung development — what drug is it?
Betamethasone is a steroid medication. It can be taken by mouth, injected into a muscle, or applied to the skin, typically in cream, lotion, or liquid forms.

Developed in Germany from the Old English Bulldog and the now-extinct Bullenbeisser, this medium-to-large mastiff-type dog breed is known for its square muzzle, underbite, and powerful bite — name the breed?
Boxer (dog breed) is a medium to large, short-haired dog breed of mastiff-type, developed in Germany.

One species in this genus of flowering shrubs, native to southern China and Indochina, has its leaves processed into the world's tea, while thousands of ornamental cultivars exist for the garden. Name the genus?
Camellia is a genus of flowering plants in the family Theaceae.
A secondarily aquatic clade within the order that also includes hippos, this infraorder covers whales, dolphins and porpoises, along with extinct relatives like Basilosaurus — which group of animals?

Cetacean are marine mammals belonging to the infraorder Cetacea, a secondarily aquatic clade under the order Artiodactyla that include whales, dolphins, porpoises and extinct groups such as Basilosaurus.
This tangor — a mandarin-orange cross — typically splits into seven to fourteen easy-to-peel segments — which fruit?
Clementine (Citrus clementina) is a tangor, a citrus fruit hybrid between a willowleaf mandarin orange (C. deliciosa) and a sweet orange (C. sinensis).
Made up of subregions called the genu, rostrum, trunk, and splenium, this thick nerve tract lets the brain's two hemispheres communicate — what is it?
Corpus callosum (Latin for "tough body"), also callosal commissure, is a wide, thick nerve tract, consisting of a flat bundle of commissural fibers, beneath the cerebral cortex in the brain.

Known by names ranging from the clinical to the crude to the childish — 'number two', 'dropping a deuce', 'doo-doo' — this basic biological process expels solid waste from the digestive tract. Name the process?

Defecation (or defaecation) follows digestion and is the necessary biological process by which organisms eliminate a solid, semisolid, or liquid waste material known as feces (or faeces) from the digestive tract via the anus or cloaca.
Best known for a single spiky, strong-smelling fruit beloved across Southeast Asia, this plant genus also includes eight other species with edible fruit — which genus?
Durio is a genus of plants in the family Malvaceae.

This broad set of measures — taken by individuals, advocacy groups, and governments alike — aims to prevent pollution, conserve natural resources, and maintain ecological balance, sometimes repairing existing damage — what is it called?
Environmental protection refers to the taking of measures to protecting the natural environment, prevent pollution and maintain ecological balance.
A legume plant from the family Fabaceae, its leaves and seeds have been common in dishes from the Indian subcontinent since ancient times — what is it?
Fenugreek (Trigonella foenum-graecum) is an annual plant in the family Fabaceae, with leaves consisting of three small obovate to oblong leaflets.
Home to the supermassive black hole known as Sagittarius A*, this point roughly 26,000 light-years from Earth marks the barycenter around which the Milky Way rotates — what is it?
Galactic Center is the barycenter of the Milky Way and a corresponding point on the rotational axis of the galaxy.

This small freshwater fish, native to China and one of the world's most popular aquarium pets, has become an invasive pest after being released into wild waterways in North America and Australia — what fish is it?
Goldfish (Carassius auratus) is a freshwater fish in the family Cyprinidae of the order Cypriniformes.

This now-outdated astronomical model placed the Sun rather than the Earth at the center of the universe, eventually replacing the geocentric view before itself being superseded by relativity — what model is it?
Heliocentrism (also known as the heliocentric model) is a superseded astronomical model that placed the Sun at the center of the universe, with the Earth and the planets in its orbit.
With atomic number 1, this element's most common isotope holds just one proton and one electron, and it's what stars like the Sun mainly burn — what is it?
Hydrogen is a chemical element; it has the symbol H and atomic number 1.
Many plants stockpile this energy-storing polysaccharide in their roots instead of starch, and doctors still use it as the benchmark substance for testing kidney function — name the fiber?
Inulin are a group of naturally occurring polysaccharides produced by many types of plants, industrially most often extracted from chicory.
This English scientist's 1808 book proposed that elements consist of identical atoms combining in fixed whole-number ratios, laying the groundwork for modern atomic theory — who is he?
John Dalton (5 or 6 September 1766 - 27 July 1844) was an English chemist, physicist, and meteorologist whose work laid the foundations of modern atomic theory and stoichiometric chemistry.
This unit of speed equals exactly one nautical mile per hour, roughly 1.15 mph, and is the standard measure used in maritime and aviation contexts — what is it called?
Knot (unit) is a unit of speed equal to one nautical mile per hour, exactly 1.852 km/h (approximately 1.151 mph or 0.514 m/s).
Found in the support tissues of most plants, this polymer resists rot and reinforces wood and bark structure — what is it?
Lignin is a class of complex organic polymers that form key structural materials in the support tissues of most plants.
This genus of Old World monkeys includes 23 species ranging from Asia and North Africa all the way to Gibraltar, and mostly eats fruit — what is it?
Macaque (Macaca) of gregarious Old World monkeys of the subfamily Cercopithecinae.
This cone-shaped structure at the base of the brainstem controls involuntary functions from heart rate and breathing to vomiting and sneezing — what is it called?
Medulla oblongata is a long stem-like structure which makes up the lower part of the brainstem.
Some of these tiny eight-legged arachnids live in soil as decomposers, others on plants causing galls, and one destructive parasite targets honeybee colonies — what are they?
Mite are small arachnids (eight-legged arthropods) of two large orders, the Acariformes and the Parasitiformes, which were historically grouped together in the subclass Acari.
This leafy Brassica rapa crop, native to the area around Beijing, became a widespread vegetable across Europe, the Americas, and Australia in the 1900s — which vegetable?
Napa cabbage (Brassica rapa subsp. In much of the world, it is referred to as "Chinese cabbage".
What's the name for the scholarly study and collection of coins, paper money, tokens and medals — though by its rules, cigarettes traded in prison don't count?
Numismatics is the study or collection of currency, including coins, tokens, paper money, medals, and related objects.
Jointly built by Italy, the UK and Germany, this variable-sweep-wing combat aircraft comes in strike, electronic-warfare and interceptor variants — which jet?
Panavia Tornado is a family of twin-engine, variable-sweep wing multi-role combat aircraft, jointly developed and manufactured by Italy, the United Kingdom and Germany.
Which management theorist and educator's writings on organizing business, government, and nonprofit sectors made him one of the most influential thinkers on modern management?

Peter Drucker (November 19, 1909 - November 11, 2005) was an Austrian American management consultant, educator, and author, whose writings contributed to the philosophical and practical foundations of modern management theory.
Known as greater plantain, this Eurasian-native flowering plant is often confused by name with a banana relative, despite no real botanical connection between the two. Which species is it?
Plantago major is a species of flowering plant in the plantain family Plantaginaceae.
A byproduct of natural gas processing and petroleum refining, this three-carbon gas becomes liquid under pressure and is a key component of the fuel sold as LPG — what compound is it?
Propane is a three-carbon chain alkane with the molecular formula C3H8.

Distinguished from their smaller rodent cousins mainly by size, these long-tailed rodents span dozens of genera worldwide, with Rattus being the most familiar — of the 56 known species, what are they collectively called?
Rat are various medium-sized, long-tailed rodents.
Discovered in 1973 by Ruth Bishop via electron micrographs, this virus is the leading cause of diarrheal disease in infants worldwide, spread via the fecal-oral route — what is it?
Rotavirus are the most common cause of diarrhoeal disease among infants and young children.
Central nervous system depressants in this drug class are often grouped with hypnotics, though technically they're meant to calm rather than induce sleep — what class of drug is this?
Sedative is a substance that induces sedation by reducing irritability or excitement.
This discipline scientifically examines human society, scaling from micro-level individual interactions up to macro-level social systems — what is it?

Sociology is the scientific study of human society that focuses on society, human social behavior, patterns of social relationships, social interaction, and aspects of culture associated with everyday life.
Lacking the powder down that herons and ibises use to clean off fish slime, these bill-clattering wading birds come in 20 living species across six genera — which birds?
Stork are large, long-legged, long-necked wading birds with long, stout bills.
This protective cap of repetitive nucleotide sequences guards the ends of eukaryotic chromosomes from progressive degradation — what is it called?
Telomere (from Ancient Greek (tlos) 'end' and (mros) 'part') is a region of repetitive nucleotide sequences associated with specialized proteins at the ends of linear chromosomes (see Sequences).
A nasty complication of this inflamed-throat illness goes by the wonderfully old-fashioned name 'quinsy,' or peritonsillar abscess — what's the underlying condition?
Tonsillitis is inflammation of the tonsils in the upper part of the throat.
Occasionally causing hearing loss or bone marrow suppression as side effects, this IV antibiotic treats MRSA infections and, in oral form, a common gut infection - which drug?
Vancomycin is a glycopeptide antibiotic medication used to treat certain bacterial infections.

This genus of four woody, twining vine species in the legume family is native across East Asia and parts of North America, and became a popular ornamental after being introduced to Europe — what genus is it?
Wisteria is a genus of flowering plants in the legume family, Fabaceae (Leguminosae).
Also known by his Latinized name Rhazes, this Persian polymath authored over 200 manuscripts on medicine, philosophy, and astronomy during the Islamic Golden Age — who was he?
Abu Bakr al-Razi: 10th-century Iranian physician and polymath.
Based on a civilian widebody jet, this European aerial-refueling tanker holds over 90% of the air-to-air refueling market outside the United States, with 17 countries as customers — which aircraft?

Airbus A330 MRTT: Aerial refuelling tanker aircraft. The Airbus A330 Multi Role Tanker Transport (MRTT) is a European aerial refueling and military transport aircraft based on the civilian Airbus A330.
About one-third the density of steel, this soft, nonmagnetic, silver-looking metal grows a protective oxide skin the instant it meets air — which element, symbol Al?
Aluminium: Chemical element with atomic number 13 (Al)
Triggered by either histamine or bradykinin, this rapid swelling of the deep skin layers can affect the face, tongue, or airway within minutes — what is it?
Angioedema: Disease characterized by rapid swelling.
Nicknamed the strawberry tree for its red berries, this evergreen Mediterranean shrub is the national tree of Italy — which plant?
Arbutus unedo: Species of flowering plant in the heather family.
The third-largest fish in its family, behind Siberian taimen and Pacific Chinook, this species is unusual for surviving spawning and returning to sea to breed again — which fish?
Atlantic salmon: Species of fish. The Atlantic salmon (Salmo salar) is a species of ray-finned fish in the family Salmonidae.
Also called the lammergeier, this bird of prey is the only known vertebrate whose diet is 70 to 90 percent bone — which bird?
Bearded vulture: Species of bird. The bearded vulture (Gypaetus barbatus), also known as the lammergeier and ossifrage, is a very large bird of prey in the monotypic genus Gypaetus.
This portmanteau of 'binary digit' is the most basic unit of information in computing, representing one of two possible states like 0 or 1 — eight of them make up a byte. What is it?
Bit: Unit of information. The bit represents a logical state with one of two possible values.
Formerly called the Russian Wolfhound until 1936, this Russian sighthound breed was originally used for hunting wolves. What breed is it?
Unlike benzodiazepines, this anti-anxiety medication doesn't cause sedation or dependence, and works through serotonin 5-HT1A receptors with a delayed onset of two to four weeks — which drug?
Buspirone: Medication used to treat anxiety disorders.
The largest living rodent, this semiaquatic South American grass-grazer lives in sociable herds of 10 to 20 — sometimes up to a hundred — near rivers and ponds; what is it?
A Turkish geologist honored by academies from the US to Russia to Serbia, he received the Gustav-Steinmann-Medaille, geology's top German prize. Who is he?
Celâl Şengör: Turkish scientist, geologist. Ali Mehmet Celâl Şengör (Turkish: [ˈali ˈmehmet ˈdʒeɫal ˈʃænɟœɾ]; born 24 March 1955) is a Turkish geologist.
A sweet-smelling, colorless solvent now made as a precursor to refrigerants and Teflon, this organochloride once served as an inhaled anesthetic from the 19th century onward — what is it?
Chloroform: CHCl3, historical anaesthetic and common solvent.
This process turns blood from liquid to gel through platelet activation and fibrin formation, beginning almost instantly after a vessel is injured — what's the clotting process called?
Coagulation: Process of formation of blood clots. Coagulation, also known as clotting, is the process by which blood changes from a liquid to a gel forming a blood clot.

This physical law holds that within an isolated system, nothing is created or destroyed — only transformed, as when a stick of dynamite converts stored chemical potential into heat, sound, and motion — what law is it?
Conservation of energy: Law of physics and chemistry.
A creeping vine of the gourd family that originated across India, Nepal, and southern China, this plant comes in slicing, pickling, and seedless types — what is it?
Cucumber: Species of flowering plant with edible fruits.

This acute medical syndrome develops over hours or days and causes disturbed attention, awareness, and sometimes hallucinations — often triggered by illness, substances, or their withdrawal — what is it called?
Delirium: Severe confusion that develops quickly, and often fluctuates in intensity.
The first species humans ever domesticated — over 14,000 years ago, before farming even began — this descendant of wolves later evolved to thrive on a starchy diet. What is it?
Dog: Domesticated species of canid. The dog (Canis familiaris or Canis lupus familiaris) is a domesticated descendant of wolves.
After stints at the CIA, Dell, and Booz Allen Hamilton, this NSA contractor flew to Hong Kong in 2013 and leaked thousands of classified documents exposing global surveillance — who is he?
Edward Snowden: Whistleblower and NSA contractor (born 1983)
One of the four basic animal tissue types, this thin protective cell layer lines blood vessels and body cavities and includes the skin's outer layer — what is it called?
Epithelium: Tissue lining the surfaces of organs in animals.
In this small bird of prey, females can be up to 25% larger than males — one of the biggest size gaps between sexes of any bird — and it hunts garden songbirds across Europe and Asia — which raptor?

Eurasian sparrowhawk: Species of bird. The Eurasian sparrowhawk (Accipiter nisus), also known as the northern sparrowhawk or simply the sparrowhawk, is a small bird of prey in the family Accipitridae.
Made by nearly every living organism, this protein locks iron away in a safe, soluble form inside cells, and its blood level is the standard test doctors use for anemia or iron overload — what is it?
Ferritin: Iron-carrying protein. Ferritin is a universal intracellular and extracellular protein that stores iron and releases it in a controlled fashion.
This Italian-American economist taught at MIT's Sloan School and Carnegie Mellon before collecting the 1985 Nobel Memorial Prize in Economics. Who was he?
Franco Modigliani: Italian-American economist and Nobel Laureate (1918–2003)

Sold under a non-proprietary name once the original patent expires, this type of medication shares the same active ingredient as its brand-name predecessor, though packaging and coloring may differ — what's it called?
Generic drug: Pharmaceutical equivalent to a brand-name product.
Despite its common name, this Eurasian wolf-like canid is more closely related to wolves and coyotes than to its African namesakes — what animal is it?
Born Herman Mudgett and dubbed the 'Beast of Chicago,' this con artist and serial killer worked his most notorious crimes around the 1893 World's Columbian Exposition — who was he?
H. H. Holmes: American con artist and serial killer (1861–1896)
Dubbed 'the Gauss of modern mathematics,' this French polymath's work on the three-body problem uncovered the first chaotic deterministic system, laying the groundwork for chaos theory — who is he?
Henri Poincaré: French mathematician, physicist and engineer (1854–1912)
With red compound eyes set wider apart in females, this insect lays batches of about 100 eggs on decaying matter that hatch into maggots — which species?
Housefly: Species of insect. The housefly (Musca domestica) is a fly of the suborder Cyclorrhapha.
Once down to just 94 individuals in Andalusia by 2002, largely due to a crash in its rabbit prey from myxomatosis, this medium-sized wild cat is endemic to a European peninsula — which species?
Iberian lynx: Species of mammal. The Iberian lynx (Lynx pardinus) is one of four extant species of Lynx, a genus of medium-sized wild cats.
This 12th-century polymath from Mesopotamia wrote a treatise describing 50 ingenious mechanical devices, including his famous elephant clock, earning him the title 'father of robotics' — who is he?
Ismail al-Jazari: Muslim engineer and artist (1136–1206)
As chief engineer, this man designed the Mitsubishi A6M Zero, Japan's iconic World War II fighter plane, and later worked on the postwar NAMC YS-11 airliner — who is he?
A founder of modern geometric analysis, this American mathematician won the 2019 Abel Prize for pioneering work in geometric partial differential equations and gauge theory — who is she?
He served as U.S. Treasury Secretary, ran the National Economic Council, and was the 27th president of Harvard before resigning his professorship there in 2026. Which economist is this?
Named after the Italian word for lemon, this citrus-scented compound comes in two mirror-image forms — one smelling of oranges, the other like pine — what is it?

Born into one of Europe's richest families in Vienna, this philosopher studied under Bertrand Russell at Cambridge before giving away his inheritance and enlisting in the Austro-Hungarian Army — who is he?
Ludwig Wittgenstein: Austrian philosopher and logician (1889–1951)
Grown as the source of the tropical mango fruit, this evergreen tree in the cashew family can reach 30 meters tall and comes in two genetic types — what species is it?
Mangifera indica: Species of flowering plant in the cashew family Anacardiaceae.
Combined with formaldehyde to create hardwearing resins found in Formica countertops, plastic dinnerware, and the foam in a Magic Eraser, this nitrogen-rich compound also resists fire — what is it?
Melamine: Fire-resistant chemical used in dinnerware, insulation, and cleaning products.
What is this — “Antiprogestogen and antiglucocorticoid drug”?
Mifepristone: Antiprogestogen and antiglucocorticoid drug. It is also used on its own to treat Cushing's syndrome or in low doses as an emergency contraceptive.
Native to tropical Central and South America, this genus of 59 flowering plant species belongs to the arum family — which genus?
Nicknamed the 'brain-eating amoeba,' this free-living microorganism lurks in warm freshwater lakes, hot springs, and poorly chlorinated pools — what is it?
A colorless gas with the formula NO, this free radical carries an unpaired electron and can be brewed by lightning in a thunderstorm. What molecule is it?
Nitric oxide: Colorless gas with the formula NO. Nitric oxide (nitrogen oxide, nitrogen mono-oxide, or nitrogen monoxide) is a colorless gas with the formula NO.
First described in 1689 by a local naturalist, this aquatic cave-dwelling salamander is the only exclusively cave-dwelling chordate native to Europe — what is it?
Britain, Germany, and Italy jointly built this twin-engine, variable-sweep-wing combat jet through a tri-national consortium, first flying it in 1974 — which aircraft?
Panavia Tornado: Family of multi-role combat aircraft.

Famous for the giant throat pouch beneath its long beak, this large water bird's eight living species range from the tropics to temperate zones, with some even flying inland to Australia's Red Centre after heavy rains — what bird is this?
Pelican: Genus of large water birds with a throat pouch.
This toxic gas, which smells like freshly cut hay, was responsible for tens of thousands of deaths as a chemical weapon in World War I — what is it?
Brightly colored as a warning sign, these diurnal tropical amphibians of Central and South America brew their toxicity from a diet of ants, mites, and termites — what's this group of frogs?
Poison dart frog: Family of amphibians.

Derived from arachidonic acid and containing a distinctive 5-carbon ring among its 20 carbons, this lipid compound can trigger opposite effects in different body tissues. What hormone-like substance is it?
Prostaglandin: Group of physiologically active lipid compounds.
Its thick bark gets harvested every 9 to 12 years for wine-bottle stoppers and cricket-ball cores — what species of oak, native to southwest Europe and Africa, is this?
Quercus suber: Species of plant. Quercus suber, commonly called the cork oak, is a medium-sized, evergreen oak tree in the section Quercus sect.

This dimensionless ratio of inertial to viscous forces predicts whether fluid flow will be smooth and laminar or chaotic and turbulent, and is used everywhere from pipe flow to aircraft wings — what is it?
Reynolds number: Ratio of inertial to viscous forces acting on a liquid.
Also called baked-apple berry or Arctic berry, this amber-hued fruit resembling a blackberry grows wild across boreal forests and Arctic tundra — what's its scientific name?
Rubus chamaemorus: Species of flowering plant in the rose family.
This large, rainbow-plumed parrot native to the forests of Central and South America is the national bird of Honduras — what is it?
Scarlet macaw: Species of bird. Like its relative the blue-and-yellow macaw, the scarlet macaw is a popular bird in aviculture as a result of its striking plumage.

Though crustaceans within this food category are more closely related to insects and spiders than to true fish, what group — including molluscs, crustaceans, and echinoderms — ranks among the most common food allergens?
Shellfish: Culinary and fisheries term for exoskeleton-bearing aquatic invertebrates.
Nicknamed a 'truth serum' in popular culture despite dubious real-world reliability, this fast-acting barbiturate anesthetic is marketed under the brand name Pentothal — which drug?
Sodium thiopental: Barbiturate general anesthetic. It is the thiobarbiturate analog of pentobarbital, and an analog of thiobarbital.
This English clergyman was the first person ever to measure blood pressure, and on the side he invented a ventilator and even wrote a tract against drinking — who was he?
Stephen Hales: English clergyman and scientist (1677–1761)
Native to tropical Africa, this berry's glycoprotein — called miraculin — tricks your tongue into tasting sour foods like lemons and limes as sweet; what is this plant commonly nicknamed?
Synsepalum dulcificum: Plant from West Africa with a taste-modifying berry.

This congenital heart defect combines four distinct abnormalities — including a hole between the ventricles and a narrowed pulmonary exit — and can trigger cyanotic 'spells' in infants — what is this condition?
Tetralogy of Fallot: Type of congenital heart defect. Tetralogy of Fallot (TOF), formerly known as Steno-Fallot tetralogy, is a congenital heart defect characterized by four specific cardiac defects.
This white compound found in sunscreen, paint, and food coloring under the number E171 makes up two-thirds of all pigments used worldwide and is valued at over $13 billion — what is it?
Titanium dioxide: Chemical compound. Titanium dioxide, also known as titanium(IV) oxide or titania, is the inorganic compound derived from titanium with the chemical formula TiO2.

These simple-looking marine invertebrates surprise biologists: their tadpole-like larvae sport a notochord and dorsal nerve cord, making them startlingly close kin to vertebrates. What are these chordates?
Tunicate: Marine animals, subphylum of chordates.
Released from the posterior pituitary when body fluids get too concentrated, this hormone helps kidneys reabsorb water and may also influence pair bonding — what is it?
